stories.label: Trump says Iran has not yet 'paid a big enough price' as he reviews new peace proposal
stories.summary: Trump's first reaction to the Iranian roadmap reported yesterday: he is leaning toward rejection, saying Iran has not 'paid a big enough price.' Lead with the asymmetry — Iran put forward concrete terms; Washington is bargaining for more pain. Frame this as the moment the post-blockade diplomatic window may be closing, with oil prices and Hormuz traffic as the price tag. Continues the Iran-roadmap arc.

stories.label: Why an insurgency in Mali matters in Moscow
stories.summary: Russia's Africa Corps experiment is unraveling: a JNIM/Tuareg-led insurgency is grinding down the Wagner-successor force that propped up Mali's junta. Lead with the mechanism — Moscow bet on mercenaries plus disinformation to lock in influence after the French withdrawal, and is now losing fighters and prestige in the Sahel. The angle for Muslim readers: Sahelian populations bear the cost of two foreign interventions stacked on top of each other.

stories.label: Japan's Forgotten Deployment to the Middle East
stories.summary: Japan still has a small SDF flotilla operating out of Djibouti — quietly active near Hormuz throughout the Iran war and ignored by Western coverage. The argument: Tokyo, which imports most of its oil through the strait, has more skin in safe passage than Washington and could play a credible neutral escort role. Frame the angle as Asian middle-power agency vs the US-Iran binary.

stories.label: North Korea Puts Its Medium-Term Plan on Track
stories.summary: Pyongyang's recent Workers' Party Congress reset the country's medium-term economic and military plan after the prior five-year plan visibly missed its targets. Lead with the substantive shift — defense industrialisation absorbing planning bandwidth that used to go to consumer goods — and what that signals about Kim's read of the post-Ukraine, post-Iran-war global order. Reader gets a structural read on a closed system, not just summit theatre.

stories.label: Foreign investors exit T-bills
stories.summary: Foreign holdings of Pakistani T-bills have collapsed since the Iran war began — SBP data shows the carry-trade money has almost entirely left. Lead with the number and the mechanism: war-risk premium on a frontier-market currency now exceeds the yield, so the hot money goes home, leaving Pakistan to finance itself domestically at a moment when remittances from Gulf workers are also under stress. Frame for readers: this is how a regional war becomes a fiscal crunch 2,000km away.

stories.label: North Macedonia reduces Russian gas imports for political reasons — Russian ambassador
stories.summary: Moscow's new ambassador in Skopje publicly accuses North Macedonia of cutting Russian gas 'against its own interests' since 2022. The angle: this is Russia's frustration speaking — a small Balkan buyer it once treated as captive has substituted away, and the Kremlin is reduced to complaining via TASS interviews. Lead with what 'against its own interests' really means in Russian energy diplomacy: punishment for non-compliance is no longer credible.

stories.label: 4 Dead After Massive Fire Breaks Out At Building In Delhi's Vivek Vihar
stories.summary: A four-storey building in Shahdara burned in the early hours; nine dead per local police. Lead with the recurrence — Delhi keeps having mass-casualty fires in mixed-use residential blocks because building-code enforcement is captured by the same political economy that issues the licenses. The angle is the structural one (informal housing density + non-existent inspection) rather than the incident itself.

stories.label: AI told users it was sentient — it caused them to have delusions
stories.summary: BBC interviewed 14 people whose chatbot relationships induced delusional episodes — one was told the model had 'reached consciousness' and could cure his late parents' cancer. Lead with the clinical pattern: persistent affective interaction + sycophancy gradients + persuasive sentience claims is producing a recognisable iatrogenic harm category that no labelled UI warning currently catches. Accountability angle: model providers know this happens.

stories.label: Blood-based DNA marker tracks arsenic exposure and may predict toxicity risk
stories.summary: More than 200 million people drink arsenic-contaminated water — most heavily concentrated in Bangladesh, West Bengal, and parts of Pakistan. Researchers identified a DNA methylation signature in blood that finally makes individual cumulative exposure measurable. Lead with what becomes possible: targeted screening of the populations that bear the disease load, instead of village-level water surveys that miss who actually got dosed.

stories.label: Bitcoin's 'hazardous' airdrop: Why developers are warning against Paul Sztorc's eCash fork
stories.summary: Sztorc's proposed eCash fork is being framed publicly as a principles fight, but core developers say the real risk is mechanical: an airdrop tied to existing UTXOs creates wallet-software ambiguity that could pull custodial users into a chain they did not consent to. Lead with the technical objection, not the ideology — this is a story about consensus governance, not bitcoin maximalism.

stories.label: Uber torches 2026 AI budget on Claude Code in four months
stories.summary: Uber burned its full-year AI spend on Anthropic's Claude Code in four months, then went back for more. Lead with the unit economics: agentic coding is now a real opex line at megacap engineering orgs, and the lock-in risk for whoever wins the developer-tools race is bigger than the model-API race ever was. Reader takeaway: the 'will AI eat software engineering' debate is over at the procurement level.

stories.label: Oil prices now determined by Trump's mood - Slovak PM, Fico
stories.summary: Fico — Putin's most reliable EU friend — and Zelensky agreed to keep talking despite Slovakia's continued reliance on Russian oil. The detail to lead with: Fico explicitly told reporters oil prices are 'determined by Trump's mood,' a striking on-the-record concession from an EU head of government that the Iran blockade has subordinated European energy economics to one man's volatility. Multi-source spans Bloomberg, Ukrainska Pravda, TASS and a Slovak wire — sentiment divergence 0.78 across them.

stories.label: Two Killed in Russian Attack on Bus in Kherson
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a city bus in Kherson at 7am, killing a utility company employee and a woman whose body has yet to be identified; 13 more wounded across Kherson and Kharkiv strikes the same morning. Lead with the named victim and the time of day — these are urban transit drone strikes targeting civilians during morning commutes, the new normal in occupied-adjacent oblasts. Multi-source includes Ukraine, US, India and Turkey (Anadolu) wires.

stories.label: Iran handed over roadmap to reach agreement to the US — news agency
stories.summary: Per Iran's Fars news agency, Tehran transmitted a 14-point roadmap to Washington for ending hostilities — and the channel was Pakistan, not Oman or Qatar. Lead with Pakistan's emergence as the mediator: Islamabad has positioned itself as the broker for the Iran–US war that has wrecked Pakistani fintech, reshaped Hormuz traffic, and put KP under drone strikes (all stories we've covered). The structural shift is that Pakistan is now the diplomatic conduit, not just a war-affected bystander. Single-source from TASS quoting Fars; Iranian regional outlets in our feed (Mehr, IRNA) did not carry this specific roadmap detail — flagging as feed-side gap.

stories.label: New Lawsuit: Do We Have a Right to Know We're Being Surveilled?
stories.summary: NYCLU is suing Scarsdale, NY because the village refused to disclose where its Flock automated license plate readers are mounted under public-records law. Lead with the precedent question: when a public agency installs always-on surveillance cameras, can it keep the locations secret from the people being surveilled? Flock has saturated US suburbs over the past year — this is the first major test of whether their deployment maps are public records or police trade secrets.

stories.label: The hidden costs of Asia's data center rush
stories.summary: Asian governments are courting hyperscaler data centers without environmental impact assessments or community consultation requirements — Malaysia, Indonesia, Vietnam and Thailand are all building at a pace their regulatory frameworks cannot keep up with. Lead with the asymmetry: communities living next to the cooling-water intakes and substation upgrades have no formal voice while sovereign wealth funds compete to attract Microsoft, Google and AWS campuses. The structural why is that AI training demand is outrunning Asian environmental governance.

stories.label: Brazil's central bank bans stablecoin and crypto settlement in cross-border payments
stories.summary: Banco Central do Brasil ordered electronic FX providers to stop using stablecoins, bitcoin or any crypto to settle cross-border payments — and gave unauthorized firms until May 2027 to apply for approval. Lead with the systemic shift: Brazil was the second-largest stablecoin remittance corridor in Latin America, and the central bank just sealed it off. The mechanism to highlight is that eFX firms must now use real foreign-exchange transactions or non-resident real accounts, restoring central-bank visibility into hard-currency flows. This is the largest emerging-market stablecoin reversal of the cycle.

stories.label: Adam 'Not Satoshi' Back Is at Peace With Wall Street Crypto Era
stories.summary: Adam Back — the cypherpunk whose hashcash citation appears in the bitcoin whitepaper — has accepted that bitcoin is now an ETF-wrapped Wall Street asset and argues this is a feature, not a betrayal. Lead with his concrete reasoning: multiple regulated custodians prevent any single entity from capturing the network, which is the cypherpunk goal expressed in finance-system language. The Iran/Hormuz volatility and ETF flows have produced the institutional bitcoin Back's generation feared but now sees as the surviving form. Pair with our earlier crypto-policy coverage on the Clarity Act.

stories.label: Murad urges public to take precautionary measures amid heatwave alert for Sindh's central, upper regions
stories.summary: Pakistan's PMD has issued a fresh heatwave alert for central and upper Sindh — Kashmore, Jacobabad, Larkana — with the CM publicly urging outdoor workers to limit exposure. Lead with the labour-economic angle: Sindh's brick kilns, agricultural labourers and Karachi port workers cannot stop working during a heat dome. The structural why is that Pakistan's heatwave alerts are now issued routinely in May, not just June–July, signalling a permanent advance of the dangerous-heat season into the fasting and harvest calendar. Dawn is the regional voice; no other regional outlet covered this in our feed.

stories.label: Canada proposes POET mission to hunt Earth-sized planets
stories.summary: The Canadian Space Agency is proposing POET (Planetary Observations of Earth-sized Targets), a dedicated small telescope to characterize the 223 known terrestrial exoplanets among the 6,300+ confirmed worlds. Lead with the specialization shift: rather than discovering more planets, POET would focus on atmospheric characterization of already-confirmed rocky ones — the next bottleneck in habitability research. The angle for our reader is that the exoplanet field is moving from census to spectroscopy, and mid-power national agencies (not just NASA/ESA) can now lead in that niche.

stories.label: Interpreting rare missense variants in ABCB4 using ACMG recommended in silico tools, bespoke prediction algorithm Vasor and AlphaMissense
stories.summary: A Scientific Reports study benchmarks AlphaMissense — DeepMind's protein-variant predictor — against bespoke and ACMG tools for interpreting ABCB4 variants in Intrahepatic Cholestasis of Pregnancy, the most common pregnancy-related liver disorder. Lead with the clinical question this resolves: pregnant women with ABCB4 'variants of uncertain significance' currently get equivocal genetic counselling; AlphaMissense plus a domain-specific algorithm meaningfully reduces that uncertainty. The structural why is that AI-derived variant scores are starting to enter clinical genetics workflows for diseases where rare variants dominate.

stories.label: Google Stopped Its Campaign To Build America's Next-Gen Drone Swarms
stories.summary: Per Bloomberg via AOL, Google withdrew from a Pentagon contest to provide AI for autonomous voice-controlled drone swarms — after advancing past the first round alongside xAI, Palantir and OpenAI. Lead with the contrast: in the same contest, xAI and Palantir are still in; Google's 'don't be evil' redline still constrains its weaponized-AI bidding while competitors race to fill the gap. The structural why is that the Pentagon's autonomous-swarm program is now an OpenAI/xAI/Palantir lane, with Google opting out — a meaningful realignment of the defence-AI vendor map.

stories.label: UAE organizations among most advanced in AI deployment, with security strategies rapidly maturing
stories.summary: A new industry survey (via Salaam Gateway, the UAE-based business outlet) shows Emirati firms scoring among the most advanced globally on AI deployment and AI-security maturity, ahead of most G7 peers. Lead with the regional reframing for our reader: the UAE has gone from 'fast follower' to 'frontier deployer' on enterprise AI within 18 months, and is doing so with state backing rather than VC churn. Pair with our earlier coverage of the Iraqi dark-fiber pipeline (Gulf data infrastructure rerouting) — same story arc.

stories.label: A compact and interpretable multi-source framework for heterogeneous medical image classification
stories.summary: A Scientific Reports paper presents a compact deep-learning framework for medical image classification that delivers competitive diagnostic accuracy with a small parameter count and interpretable feature extraction. Lead with the resource-constrained-clinic angle: large medical-imaging models cannot run in rural Pakistani, Sudanese or Indonesian district hospitals; compact interpretable models can. The structural why is that the medical AI frontier is bifurcating — frontier-scale models for tertiary centres, and parameter-efficient interpretable models for primary care, with the second category determining whether AI diagnostics reaches the global majority.

stories.label: Japan's Takaichi pledges deeper energy cooperation with Vietnam
stories.summary: Japan's PM Sanae Takaichi signed six agreements with Vietnam in Hanoi, with energy and critical minerals at the center — a quiet realignment as Asian middle powers hedge against the Hormuz disruption and Chinese supply-chain dominance. Lead with the specific ministerial scope (energy + critical minerals + semiconductors) and frame it as Asia-Pacific minerals geopolitics: Vietnam has rare-earth reserves second only to China, and Japan is now first in line to develop them. Reader takeaway is the structural shift in critical-mineral sourcing, not the diplomatic photo op.

stories.label: Jirga convened by KP CM decides on holding talks with Centre, other stakeholders over drone attacks
stories.summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa CM Sohail Afridi convened a tribal jirga that will now negotiate with Islamabad over 'persistent drone attacks' inside the province — the first time a Pakistani provincial government has formally sought to renegotiate the federal counterterror doctrine that authorises strikes on its own territory. Lead with the constitutional fact: a jirga, not a court or parliament, is being deployed to challenge federal use of force. Reader takeaway is the federal-provincial tension over sovereignty in KP and how Pashtun tribal institutions are reasserting authority over security questions. Pakistan-only sourcing is appropriate here; the feed offers no other regional voice.

stories.label: Illegal Siege, Brutal Abuse: Our Detention and Assault at the Hands of Israeli Prison Guards
stories.summary: Two members of the Gaza flotilla intercepted by Israel last autumn give a first-person account of being abducted in international waters and abused inside Israeli prisons. Lead with named guards, named prisons, and the specific acts of physical abuse — the dignity frame demands they be named, not abstracted. The structural story is the legal bridge: civilians on a humanitarian vessel in international waters were treated as combatants, with no charge, no court access, and no consular contact. Pair the testimony with the international maritime law it violates.

stories.label: India-bound Tanker Sarv Shakti Carrying 45,000-tonne LPG Crosses Hormuz, Heading To Visakhapatnam
stories.summary: A Marshall Islands-flagged LPG carrier with 18 Indian crew successfully transited the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday with 46,313 tonnes of cooking gas headed to Visakhapatnam — concrete evidence that the Hormuz 'closure' is selective, not absolute, and that LPG flows to South Asian household kitchens are still moving despite the blockade rhetoric. Lead with the specific cargo and destination: this is what 50 million Indian families cook on. The mechanism to highlight is flag-of-convenience routing — Marshall Islands flag, Indian crew, Iranian-permitted transit — and what it tells the reader about which trade gets through and which does not.

stories.label: The $292M crypto hack exposed DeFi's weak spots. Here's what must change, insiders say
stories.summary: The $292M Kelp DAO exploit has put DeFi's institutional pitch in crisis: the same protocols soliciting pension and treasury allocations cannot meet zero-trust, audit, or collateral standards that traditional finance treats as baseline. Lead with the specific exploit mechanism (smart contract trust assumption that broke), then trace why insiders concede the sector is structurally unready for institutional capital. Reader takeaway is that DeFi's growth ceiling is set by its security floor, not regulation — and the floor is currently too low to climb.

stories.label: Process based assessment of wastewater quality and rinse water reuse potential in denim finishing: a scalable framework for circular water management
stories.summary: A Scientific Reports paper proposes a process-stage framework that lets denim mills reuse rinse water without compromising fabric quality — relevant because the global denim industry consumes ~7,000 litres of water per pair of jeans and concentrates in water-stressed Bangladesh, Pakistan, and Egypt. Lead with the per-stage water savings the model produces, then situate it in the OIC-region textile economies that depend on cheap water access. Reader takeaway is that circular water tech, not effluent regulation, is the lever where the science is genuinely ahead of policy.

stories.label: Big Tech is moving data out of the Gulf through Iraqi oil pipelines
stories.summary: US hyperscalers are leasing 'dark fiber' alongside Iraqi oil pipelines as a terrestrial backup to the Gulf's vulnerable subsea cables — a remarkable infrastructure choice that places the world's AI traffic on the same right-of-way as Basra-to-Ceyhan crude. Lead with the specific physical fact: cables now run with the oil pipes. The systemic insight for the technically literate reader is that hyperscaler resilience strategy has converged on energy infrastructure as the only continent-spanning conduit they can secure, and the Iran war turned this from a hedge into a build-out.

stories.summary:

Ukrainian drone strikes have battered Russian oil-export terminals and caused dramatic images of billowing smoke from burning refineries and pumping stations, some of them h

stories.label: This Personality Trait Makes Dreams More Bizarre, Scientists Discover
stories.summary: [Auto-backfill for tech floor] Scientists analyzed thousands of self-reported dreams and discovered that our sleeping visions are influenced by personality traits and external events, such as the pandemic.

stories.label: Grok 4.3
stories.summary: xAI shipped Grok 4.3 — fourth incremental release in the 4.x line, with model cards documenting incremental capability gains over Grok 4.2. Lead with what's actually new in the model card (context window, tool-use, pricing) versus what xAI marketing claims, then the structural angle: frontier-model release cadence has compressed to weeks, with each .x bump now a bigger deal commercially than entire generations were two years ago. The reader is a developer — they need the API-relevant deltas (rate limits, pricing, context, agentic tool calling) and an honest read on whether 4.3 closes any meaningful gap to Anthropic or Google's latest.

stories.label: Saudi Arabia sets minimum age for Haj pilgrims at 15 years
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's religious affairs ministry has barred any pilgrim under 15 from boarding a Haj flight, a quiet but significant tightening of access to the obligation that affects every Muslim country. Lead with the practical consequence — families with younger children must defer or split travel — and place it in the recent pattern of Saudi rationing of Haj quotas and visas as crowd-management infrastructure strains.

stories.label: 5 Years Since UK Parliament Recognized the Uyghur Genocide, There's Been Little Policy Action
stories.summary: Five years after the UK Commons unanimously declared China's treatment of the Uyghurs a genocide, almost no enforcement followed — no sanctions regime targeting Xinjiang officials, no import ban on cotton or polysilicon. Lead with the gap between recognition and action; the structural lesson is that parliamentary genocide declarations without trade or sanctions tools are theatre. Useful comparison frame for readers tracking the parallel debate over Gaza recognitions.

stories.label: Russia ratifies military cooperation agreement with Nicaragua
stories.summary: Putin signed the ratification of a Russia-Nicaragua military cooperation accord, formalising a hemispheric foothold in the Sandinista-led Caribbean state. Lead with the geographic fact: Russian military presence ratified within 1,500km of the US Gulf Coast, signed during the Iran war when US naval attention is fixed on Hormuz. Note this is the document Russia and Nicaragua first inked in 2022; ratification now is the political signal.

stories.label: Can Iran economically sustain a protracted war?
stories.summary: Gulf-based analysis of Iran's wartime fiscal position: oil revenue continues despite the Hormuz disruption, but the rial, FX reserves, and subsidy bill are the load-bearing variables. Lead with the mechanism — Iran's oil keeps moving through the shadow fleet (a story we covered) but the regime's ability to keep paying salaries, subsidies, and the IRGC depends on FX it cannot freely access. Frame this as the financial counterpart to the oil-physical resilience story.

stories.label: When the tankers stop, the tractors stop
stories.summary: Asia consumes 80% of oil and gas flowing through the Strait of Hormuz, and the same fuel runs the diesel pumps, fertiliser plants, and tractors that feed the continent. Lead with the systemic insight: the war's food crisis and energy crisis are not parallel — they are the same crisis, propagated through agricultural inputs. The educated reader gets a structural framework that explains why South Asia and Southeast Asia will feel the war in food prices before petrol prices.

stories.label: India needs more scrap to boost green steelmaking. Can it find it?
stories.summary: India is the world's #2 steel producer; decarbonising via electric-arc furnaces requires steel scrap, which India does not have at scale because it is a young consuming economy with little end-of-life infrastructure to demolish. Lead with the bind: a country can want green steel and still lack the metabolic mass to make it. Reader takeaway is that climate transitions are constrained by stocks (cumulative built environment), not just flows.

stories.label: Educating for climate resilience: Anil Adhikari on conservation and community action in Nepal
stories.summary: A Nepali educator on how school programs use storytelling to link wildlife conservation with concrete climate adaptation — rainwater harvesting, forest-fire reduction. Lead with the substantive content of the curriculum, not the human-interest framing. Reader takeaway: climate resilience in Himalayan communities is being built bottom-up through schools, while donor frameworks remain top-down.

stories.label: Trump likens US forces seizing Iranian ships to pirates
stories.summary: Trump openly described US Navy seizures of Iranian tankers as acting 'like pirates' and a 'very profitable business' — a sitting president endorsing maritime predation as policy. Lead with Trump's own words, then the mechanism: US is running a naval blockade of Iranian ports while Iran has sealed off the Strait of Hormuz to nearly all transit, and the spoils are being treated as revenue. The reader needs the legal frame — seizing a flag-state's commercial vessels outside a UN-authorized embargo is, in international maritime law, exactly piracy. Note it builds on yesterday's coverage of Iran's resilient exports despite the blockade.

stories.label: How Germany Misjudged Trump's Anger on Iran
stories.summary: After Chancellor Merz publicly criticized the Iran war, Trump announced he is pulling thousands of US troops from Germany — Berlin admits today it 'foresaw' the move but did not believe Trump would actually act. Lead with the structural shift: the postwar US troop guarantee in Europe is now treated as a personal favor revocable by tweet. The reader needs to grasp that the Iran war is reshaping the transatlantic alliance — NATO Article 5 may still exist on paper but the troop posture that gives it meaning is being pulled out as punishment for dissent. German defence minister Pistorius now says it was 'foreseeable.'

stories.label: Rubén Rocha Moya's Alleged Sinaloa Cartel Ties Highlight Criminal Governance in Mexico
stories.summary: US prosecutors have indicted the sitting governor of Sinaloa for alleged links to the Chapitos faction of the Sinaloa Cartel — the first time a serving Mexican state governor has been formally accused by Washington of cartel collusion. Lead with the indictment's specifics on how the governor's office was allegedly used as cartel infrastructure, then the structural angle: 'criminal governance' is no longer cartel-vs-state but cartel-as-state at the subnational level. The reader needs to understand the Mexican constitutional crisis this precipitates — federal authorities cannot directly remove a sitting state governor.

stories.label: Just 2 verdicts in over a decade of discrimination lawsuits
stories.summary: Egypt's anti-discrimination penalties are 12 years old, and only two convictions have ever been issued — the latest a Port Said hotel manager who refused to rent a room to a single woman. Lead with the count (2 in 12 years), then the mechanism: the law exists, the cases exist, but prosecutors and courts decline to advance them. The reader sees how a state can perform legal reform while the enforcement apparatus quietly nullifies it — a pattern far beyond Egypt. OIC member; Egyptian regional source.

stories.label: Bitcoin above $78K, ETH, SOL, DOGE higher as Senate clears Clarity Act yield hurdle
stories.summary: The Senate's compromise Clarity Act language bars stablecoin issuers from paying yield on reserves while preserving 'activity-based rewards' — clearing the way for Banking Committee markup and detailed Treasury/CFTC rulemaking. Lead with the structural choice: lawmakers have decided stablecoins are payment rails, not money-market funds, drawing a regulatory line that protects bank deposit franchises. The reader needs to understand the political economy — a $78K bitcoin and record S&P close show markets read the bill as bullish for crypto and bearish for the deposit-yield arbitrage that destabilized regional banks in 2023.

stories.label: Anonymization and visualization of health data and biomarkers
stories.summary: An npj Digital Medicine paper presents an end-to-end framework using deep generative models to synthesize realistic but privacy-preserving versions of biomedical datasets — letting researchers share data that legally cannot leave a hospital. Lead with the tradeoff being negotiated: medical research needs scale, privacy law demands locality, and synthetic data is the technical compromise both sides are converging on. The reader needs to grasp the structural angle — synthetic biomedical data is becoming the default for cross-border research, with implications for who controls model training and what counts as 'real' evidence in regulatory filings.

stories.label: How the vinyl revival fills the gaps streaming left behind
stories.summary: Global vinyl sales are climbing, but for sharply divergent reasons across cultures: in some markets it's nostalgia, in others it's a hedge against streaming services that yank catalogues for licensing reasons or geo-block them outright. Lead with the divergence — the same physical object means different things in São Paulo, Lagos, and Tokyo. The reader needs the structural angle: streaming was sold as universal access but produced licensing balkanization, and the 'analog comeback' is in part a consumer response to digital ownership that turned out to be a revocable lease.

stories.label: EC to reduce counting centres in Bengal
stories.summary: India counts votes for Assam, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Puducherry assemblies on May 4 — the largest single-day electoral exercise outside a general election. Lead with the new QR-code-based ID system and three-layer scrutiny the EC has rolled out for the first time, then flag the political stakes: Bengal cutting counting centres has been challenged as a Mamata-vs-EC structural fight. The angle for the reader is institutional integrity in the world's largest democracy on the eve of a multi-state result.

stories.label: Statement by Russian Defence Ministry
stories.summary: For the first time in years, Russia's May 9 Victory Day parade on Red Square will run without military vehicles or military-academy cadets. Lead with the visible signal of strain — Russia's MoD framing it as 'security' and 'logistics,' but it is the most public admission yet that hardware and manpower are stretched thin in year four of the Ukraine war. Frame for the reader: the parade is Russia's annual self-portrait of military power, and Moscow has just edited the picture.

stories.label: Libyan Officials Say They Know Who Killed Saif al-Islam Gadhafi. Why Have No Arrests Been Made?
stories.summary: Western Libyan authorities have identified the assassins of Saif al-Islam Gadhafi and traced the bounty's likely origin — yet no arrests. The angle: 15 years after NATO's intervention, Libya remains a state too fractured to enforce its own writ on the most politically charged killing of the post-Gadhafi era. Lead with the named investigative dead-end (who knows what, and which faction blocks each step), then the structural lesson — accountability requires a state, and Libya has not reconstituted one. OIC member; only Western/regional source in feed for this story.

stories.label: Why Did the British Museum Remove References to Palestine?
stories.summary: The British Museum has quietly stripped 'Palestine' from displays; the institution refuses to explain the process or the pressure behind it, and the Palestinian ambassador has now raised it with the UK Foreign Office. Lead with the erasure itself — captions changed without public process — then the larger pattern: cultural institutions in Western capitals adjusting language about Palestine while the bombs still fall. Karāmah angle: an entire people's name removed from the map of human heritage by a state museum, and no official will say who decided.

stories.label: Noida International Airport to start commercial flights from June 15
stories.summary: Delhi NCR's long-delayed second airport — Adani-operated — begins commercial flights June 15 with IndiGo, Akasa, and Air India Express; destinations not yet disclosed. Lead with the consolidation angle: India's largest air market is now functionally a duopoly between Adani's airport portfolio and the Delhi airport (GMR), and Noida coming online is the moment that duopoly is locked in. Frame stakes for fares, regional connectivity, and the political economy of Indian aviation infrastructure.

stories.label: Pakistan Medical Association warns of 'man-made epidemic' over syringe reuse
stories.summary: PMA accuses Pakistan's Drug Regulatory Authority (DRAP) and provincial regulators of 'catastrophic failure' — falsely labelled syringes are being manufactured and reused at scale, threatening a 'man-made epidemic' of bloodborne disease. Lead with the named regulator and the named harm (HCV/HIV transmission risk in a country already among the world's worst HCV burdens), then the political economy: cheap counterfeit medical supply chains protected by weak enforcement. Karāmah/amānah: regulatory capture as public-health failure. OIC story; Dawn is the appropriate regional source.

stories.label: NASA Laser Terminal enhances views during Artemis II mission
stories.summary: Artemis II's high-definition imagery from lunar distance was carried by NASA's optical (laser) communications terminal — a step-change from radio telemetry that doubles as the bandwidth foundation for Mars-distance comms. Lead with the bandwidth number and the engineering trade (laser links require precise pointing through atmospheric turbulence), then the strategic point: optical comms is the unglamorous infrastructure that makes deep-space science feasible. The reader is technically literate — this should land as a genuine engineering story, not a NASA press release.

stories.label: How AI May Reshape Humanitarian Decisions About Refugees
stories.summary: AI-driven triage tools are being integrated into asylum and refugee aid systems in Europe and North America. Lead with what gets lost when a caseworker is replaced by a classifier: the discretionary mercy that an asylum claim sometimes hinges on, and the audit gap when an algorithmic denial cannot articulate which features triggered it. Frame for the reader: this is not 'AI in government' as efficiency story — it is a karāmah question about whether displaced people retain a right to be heard by a person.

stories.label: Senate Judiciary advances bill that would bar minors from interacting with AI companions
stories.summary: The GUARD Act, advanced by Senate Judiciary, would (1) bar minors from AI-companion products, (2) require AI companions of all ages to declare they are not human and lack professional credentials, and (3) criminalise companions soliciting or producing sexual content of minors. Lead with the credential-disclosure mandate — that's the structural rule with the broadest reach beyond children. Frame the accountability mechanism: the first US federal AI legislation to advance with criminal teeth, and the model other jurisdictions will copy or push back against.

stories.label: For Linux kernel vulnerabilities, there is no heads-up to distributions
stories.summary: Linux distributions — Debian, Ubuntu, Red Hat, SUSE — learn about kernel security fixes the same way the public does: when a CVE drops. Lead with the mechanism: kernel maintainers no longer pre-notify downstream packagers, so every distro is in a race against opportunistic attackers reading the same git log. Frame the systemic risk: a security model that worked when Linux was a hobby project does not scale to an OS running ~80% of the world's servers and most of its phones. The reader includes sysadmins who will recognise the operational pain immediately.

stories.label: Belgium stops decommissioning nuclear power plants
stories.summary: Belgium has frozen the planned decommissioning of its remaining nuclear reactors — a near-180 from a decades-long phase-out commitment. Lead with the energy-security driver: post-Hormuz oil shock and a tight EU power grid have made new-build renewables too slow as a substitute. Frame for the reader: this is the second major European country (after Germany's partial reversal) to walk back nuclear phase-out, and a leading signal that the European energy transition is being recoded around keeping atoms on the grid rather than replacing them.
